title: Correct refraction angle
description: Essential: Student correctly applies Snell's Law to find the refraction angle (30°) from the given incident angle (45°) and refractive index (√2).

title: Time calculation
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates the final time t = (2√6 a) / (3c) by combining the geometric path length in the medium with the speed v = c/√2.

title: Width calculation
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates the final width d = (√3 / 3) a using trigonometry (e.g., tan 30°) and the geometry of the square cross-section.

title: Geometric path analysis
description: Important: Student correctly relates the refracted ray's path length inside the block to the side length a using the refraction angle (e.g., l = a / cos 30°).

title: Speed in medium
description: Important: Student correctly uses the relationship v = c / n to find the speed of light in the glass.

title: Trigonometry for width
description: Important: Student correctly sets up the horizontal displacement from the refraction point to the edge of face CD (e.g., using tan θ = BE / a or equivalent subtraction).

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Student's final answers for time and width have correct units (s and a, respectively) or explicitly states them.

title: Misapplication of Snell's Law
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly applies Snell's Law (e.g., swaps incident and refracted angles, uses cosine instead of sine) leading to a wrong refraction angle.

title: Incorrect geometric path
description: Pitfall: Student uses an incorrect trigonometric relationship (e.g., confuses adjacent/opposite sides for path length or width calculation).

title: Algebraic or arithmetic error
description: Pitfall: Student makes a sign error, simplification mistake, or arithmetic error in the final expressions for t or d.
